sources.entry: Web Servers and Reverse Proxies. A web server is a piece of software and underlying hardware that accepts requests via HTTP (the network protocol created to distribute web content) or its secure variant HTTPS. summary.name: Reverse proxy
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article explaining the reverse proxy concept: a server that appears to clients as an ordinary web server while forwarding their requests to one or more back-end servers.
keywords: how does a reverse proxy work
use_cases: Load balancing traffic across internal web servers
Exposing several web apps behind one public IP address
Caching static and dynamic content to reduce origin load
Terminating TLS in front of backend servers
Adding authentication to a web server that lacks it
Running A/B tests without changing application code
summary.what_it_does: The page defines a reverse proxy as an intermediary that forwards client requests to one or more ordinary web servers, so the back ends can sit behind a firewall with only the proxy exposed. It lists uses including load balancing, caching, compression, TLS encryption or offloading, routing by URL or HTTP headers, and web application firewall features against DoS and DDoS attacks. It also covers risks: the proxy must decrypt traffic to inspect it, holds private keys, and is a single point of failure. The article cites a 2020 Cloudflare outage as an example.
notable: Explains the security trade-offs of reverse proxies, including TLS key exposure and single point of failure
Describes spoon-feeding, where the proxy delivers a generated page to the client so the origin server can release resources
Notes that reverse proxies can hide origin servers, which affects takedowns and legal action
caveats: Reverse proxies can read and modify non-encrypted traffic, and a compromised proxy exposes internal networks.
Giving a third-party proxy access to private keys places confidentiality, integrity and availability in that party's hands.
The proxy is a single point of failure for the back-end services it fronts.
